To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a minimal dietary vitamin B6 level of 3.0 mg per kg diet during lactation is necessary for health and development of the offspring.
a minimal maternal diet vitamin B6 supply during lactation of 3.0 mg vitamin B per kg diet is required to ensure the health and development of the offspring.
the offspring of dams with vitamin B6 deficient diets (0.2mg vitamin B6/kg diet) showed no significant changes in body weight, haematological parameters and transaminase enzyme activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of vitamin B6 deficiency during lactation on health and development of offspring.
the question whether a maternal vitamin B6 supply above 5 mg per kg diet can be considered as excessive.

the effects of a varying maternal dietary vitamin B 6 supplementation during lactational period on vitamin B 6 concentration in blood, liver, total body, and activities of two transamidation enzymes in the offspring of Sprague‐Daweley rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vitamin B6 status during lactation period of the mother is not the most important factor for the health and development of her offspring.
the maternal vitamin B6 supply is important for the health and development of offspring.

the present results indicate that the maternal dietary vitamin supply is of importance for the vitamin B6 status and the development of the offspring, but that the present results do not indicate that a vitamin B6 deficiency in the mother during lactation has a negative influence on the development and health status of the offspring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a maternal vitamin B6 supply during lactation above 3mg per kg diet is sufficient to guarantee an appropriate vitamin B6 supply in the offspring.
a minimal maternal vitamin B6 supply in the diet during lactation of 3.2 mg per kg diet seems to be necessary for a normal development of the offspring.
the offspring of rats with a deficient maternal dietary supply of vitamin B6 during lactation period show no signs of vitamin B6 deficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maternal dietary vitamin supply during lactation is a critical factor influencing the vitamin B6 concentrations and the activity of the transaminase enzymes.

the maternal dietary vitamin supplementation during lactation had a significant influence on the vitamin B6 status and on the activities of the AST and ALT in liver of the offspring, but the vitamin B6 concentrations in blood and liver as well as the activities of AST in plasma and ALT in erythrocytes were not influenced by a maternal vitamin B6 deficiency during lactation.
the maternal dietary vitamin b6 supply during lactation is an essential parameter for the vitamin B6 status and the development of the offspring.
